declarations.description:
Modal confirmation on the native `<dialog>`, with `role="alertdialog"`. It interrupts to ask
one question, so it has no close button and no light dismiss: only the two actions, or
Escape (which counts as cancel), close it. Initial focus lands on the cancel action, so a
reflexive Enter never confirms. Focus returns to the element that opened it.

The footer repeats `ht-dialog`'s signature: two flat actions flush to the bottom edge, the
confirm action first with a mixed-radius corner. The buttons are drawn locally, so this file
does not depend on `ht-button`.

open while an async action runs, then set `open = false` yourself.

the grid, arrows move by day and week, Home and End jump to the ends of the week, Page Up
and Page Down change month, Shift with them changes year, Enter or Space selects.

declarations.description:
Search box over a filtered list of commands: a combobox with a listbox, in the style of a
command palette. Items are `ht-command-item` children, optionally inside `ht-command-group`.
Typing filters them; Arrow keys move the highlight while focus stays in the search box
(`aria-activedescendant`); Enter picks.

Inline by default. With `palette`, the same content opens in a native `<dialog>` near the
top of the page: set `open`, call `show()`, or give it a `hotkey` such as `mod+k` (`mod` is
Command on Apple platforms and Control elsewhere). Escape closes it, and focus returns to
where it was.

Filtering matches each word of the query against the item text and its `keywords`, as a
substring, or (for words of 3+ letters) as the item text's letters in order. Items keep
their authored order. Groups with no match hide.

Screen readers: results are announced through a polite status region ("3 results"). Where
the browser cannot link the search box to a slotted option by reference
(`ariaActiveDescendantElement`), the highlighted option is announced there instead.

Home and End jump to the first and last result, so they do not move the text caret.

declarations.description:
Data table made of custom elements. Layout uses `display: table*` on the hosts, and each
host carries its own ARIA role (`table`, `rowgroup`, `row`, `columnheader`, `cell`), so
assistive technology sees an ordinary table. Give it an accessible name with `aria-label`.

```html
<ht-table aria-label="Projects">
  <ht-table-head><ht-table-row>
    <ht-table-header sortable key="name">Name</ht-table-header>
    <ht-table-header align="end">Events</ht-table-header>
  </ht-table-row></ht-table-head>
  <ht-table-body>
    <ht-table-row><ht-table-cell>sentinel</ht-table-cell><ht-table-cell align="end">1,204</ht-table-cell></ht-table-row>
  </ht-table-body>
</ht-table>
```

The table does not sort or filter. A sortable header fires `sort`; reorder your rows in
response. Only one header shows a sort direction at a time.

The table scrolls horizontally when it is wider than its container, and joins the
tab order while it does, so keyboard users can scroll it. For a sticky header, set
`sticky-header` and give the table a height with `--ht-table-max-height`.
